Introducing: A Cookbook That Gets the Way Your Brain Works

Some Days, you Just Need To Eat.

Cooking is freakin' hard.

Especially if you have issues with executive functioning. Planning. Organization. Time Management.

Cooking is full of EF skills. And some days we just don't have it, but we still need to eat.

How can we call ourselves Life Skills Advocate, if we don't ACTUALLY advocate for improving the accessibility of one of the most fundamental life skills of all?

Cooking.

Cooking is really hard for a lot of neurodivergent people because it requires a ton of executive functioning and most of the tools that are readily available just don't work very well.

So... what can be done about this?

If you're made of money, you can hire a personal chef, get your meals delivered, or just eat out everyday.

But unfortunately, that's not a sustainable model for most people.

So cooking (or preparing food in some form) is typically the best option most of the time.

But again, cooking is hard and causes tons of stress and anxiety.

And shame spiraling.

To relieve the stress, anxiety and shame, we go out to eat anyway even if we can't afford it or prepare something we know isn't good for us.

And then often, we experience shame around that choice as well.

It's a vicious freakin' circle where it feels like whatever choice you make, you have to sacrifice something important.

Until today.

DUN DUN DUUUUN!!!! (dramatic sound effect)

Introducing... The Real-Life Executive Functioning Cookbook.

We spent hours and hours soul searching (at least 1 of the authors is neurodivergent), listened to pain points about cooking expressed by our coaching clients, and read through countless frustrations on online forums about everything that's not neurodivergent-friendly about traditional cookbooks.

From there, we came up with a list of everything we thought we could improve upon in a reasonable amount of time.

And we set out to do just that.

Below is everything we believe our cookbook delivers to the neurodivergent community (and anyone really) that traditional cookbooks don't... with more still to come.

My hope is that our cookbook will save you some money, time, assist you in developing an important life skill, and most importantly, make cooking accessible thereby helping you realize what you're capable of.

WHAT MAKES THIS digital COOKBOOK NEURODIVERGENT-FRIENDLY?

Click here to view a sample recipe.

Zero jumping around

BASED ON

REAL LIFE

None of our recipes require you to jump to page 267 for the sauce or page 85 for the other sauce. All necessary steps are self-contained within each recipe.

Keeps you ahead of waiting PARALYSIS

TESTED IN

REAL LIFE

Overwhelmed or not sure what to do while waiting for the water to boil? We've included red bold text cues.

built in prep time

Our cookbook encourages you to retrieve all the ingredients & supplies and, when it makes sense, complete all the prep FIRST before even turning on a burner. Slower? Maybe. Less stressful and safer? Definitely.

Readiness cues

Do you sometimes ambitiously jump into a project without knowing what you're getting yourself into only to realize halfway though that you may be in over your head? Step 1 of every recipe is to "Read it Through".

Don't burn your house down reminders

Critical safety reminders like turning off the burner before walking away are called out so you don't burn your house down!

Expansion Ideas

Novelty is important! We've included a list of optional ingredients and variation ideas for each recipe in our book.

Photo examples for everything

Every step includes a photo.

Brain power meter

Look for our Brain Power Meter icons at the top of each recipe to quickly tell how much brain power it'll require.

Function First

Look... this isn't a cookbook that's going to teach you how to become Julia Child. This is a functional cookbook! While super tasty, we've intentionally prioritized recipes that anyone can cook.

Icons That Make Sense

At the top of each recipe, in addition to our Brain Power Meter, we've included a few other helpful icons to help you makes choices based on the situation, time, budget and more.

ACTION ITEMS IN BOLD 

Sometimes extra words are needed to help people understand what the hell we're talking about. Action items are always displayed in bold to help you focus in on what's most important.

CHAPTERS ORGANIZED BY

EF-DEMAND

While most cookbooks organize their chapters by cuisine, ours organizes by brain power. Running low on brain capacity? Try the "Three Ingredients or Less" chapter.

ALL INGREDIENTS ARE EASY TO FIND

No hunting down some super specific ingredient that you probably can't even tell the difference from the alternative anyway.

measurements are "split" from the beginning

You know how at the top of most cookbook recipes, they say something like "olive oil (split)" but don't tell you how much to split until you get way down to that step? That's annoying. Don't do that.

Portable & flexible

Pull the cookbook up on your phone or tablet or print out just the recipe you're working on.

ZERO PERSONAL ANECDOTES/LIFE STORIES

You're welcome.

Benefits of our cookbook

Save Time

Fewer transitions and steps means less time wasted in the kitchen and more time enjoying the delicious food you made!

Build Confidence

It's amazing what can happen when previously inaccessible skills become accessible. It often leads to greater confidence!

Save Money

It's no secret that eating out or ordering in is expensive. Save money by preparing more of your meals at home.

Learn a Valuable Life Skill

Cooking is a skill that spans beyond the right here and now. Take it with you wherever you go in life.

Who is this cookbook for?

In short, anyone can benefit from our cookbook.

However, it was specially-designed for neurodivergent individuals who struggle with executive functioning.

We believe the Real-Life Executive Functioning Cookbook is also a great tool for parents, educators, coaches, and anyone who supports neurodivergent individuals.

Print your own and fully customize your meal planning and preparation.

CHRIS HANSON  //  Author

Hi, I’m Chris and I was born and raised in Cleveland, Ohio. I moved to the Seattle area in September of 2008 and soon after, I met my awesome wife, Lisa!

I earned my special education teaching degree while working as paraeducator in the Kent School District. Overall, I have about 8 years of classroom experience and 20 years and counting of personal experience with ADHD and anxiety. I started Life Skills Advocate in 2019 because I wanted to create the type of support service I wish I had when I was a teenager struggling to find my path in life. I feel very grateful to be on the other side of it, supporting some amazing young adults.With everything I do, my mission is to provide neurodivergent individuals and families with the life skills training, executive functioning support, mentorship & coaching they need to build and sustain autonomy & independence.

Which includes cooking!

I consider the Real-Life Executive Functioning Cookbook to be a natural extension of this mission.

Chris 

AMY SIPPL  //  Author

Hi, I'm Amy, a Minnesota-based Board Certified Behavior Analyst (BCBA) and freelance content developer specializing in helping individuals with diverse learning needs and their families reach their best possible outcomes.

I earned my Masters Degree in Applied Behavior Analysis from St. Cloud State University and also hold undergraduate degrees in Psychology and Family Social Science from University of Minnesota – Twin Cities.

I have worked with children with autism and related developmental disabilities for over a decade in both in-home and clinical settings. My content focuses on parents, educators, and professionals in the world of autism—emphasizing simple strategies and tips to maximize success.

Amy

Highly recommended!

For anyone who has struggled to consume three nutritious meals a day due to executive functioning challenges, this cookbook is your guide. From meal planning to shopping list, this cookbook makes it easy. Particularly helpful is the list of recipes in the "I Just Need to Eat" section that have minimal ingredients and take minimal time (and brain power) to prepare. Speaking of brain power, I love the Brain Power Meter which indicates on each recipe how much executive functioning is required to prepare it. You can start easy and work your way up step-by-step to the most difficult, which require careful attention and the most skill and experience. Highly recommended!

Patty laushman  //  Coach & Mom

Who is This Cookbook For?

In short, anyone can benefit from our cookbook.

However, it was specially-designed for neurodivergent individuals who struggle with executive functioning.

We believe the Real-Life Executive Functioning Cookbook is also a great tool for parents, educators, coaches, and anyone who supports neurodivergent individuals.

How Many Recipes Are Included?

20 (and countless variation)

Is a physical copy Available Somewhere?

Not at this time. And we're not sure if there ever will be. All the options we've explored so far require us to give up either a huge chunk of each sale or creative control. We're not interested in doing either.

If you know of a better way to publish or self-publish, we're all ears. Reach out to me at chris@lifeskillsadvocate.com.

Can/Should I Print This Cookbook Then?

You certainly can. After purchase, the cookbook will be delivered to you as a .pdf file, and if printing is the best format for you, we'd recommend doing so.

Can I freely Distribute This Cookbook?

You are more than welcome to use our cookbook with yourself, your family, and the learners your support, however, I must ask that you NOT share it with your colleagues or other people. As well-intentioned as doing so may be, making copies of and sharing any paid product is considered stealing. We are a small company and the sales generated from this cookbook enable us to fund many of the free resources found on our website dedicated to supporting neurodiverse learners, families & professionals.

If you wish to purchase multiple cookbook licenses for your organization, please reach out to me directly at chris@lifeskillsadvocate.com and we can discuss bulk license discount options. Thank you!

Do You Accept Purchase Orders?

Yes, if your school or organization would like to purchase single or bulk licenses via purchase order, please email chris@lifeskillsadvocate.com.

What is Your Refund Policy?

You are fully protected by our 100% Satisfaction-Guarantee. If you aren't satisfied within 7 days of purchase, just let us know and we'll send you a prompt refund.

Who Can I Contact if I have questions?

Reach out anytime by emailing chris@lifeskillsadvocate.com.

Introducing: A Cookbook That Gets the Way Your Brain Works

Some Days, you Just Need To Eat.

Cooking is freakin' hard.

Especially if you have issues with executive functioning. Planning. Organization. Time Management.

Cooking is full of EF skills. And some days we just don't have it, but we still need to eat.

How can we call ourselves Life Skills Advocate, if we don't ACTUALLY advocate for improving the accessibility of one of the most fundamental life skills of all?

Cooking.

Cooking is really hard for a lot of neurodivergent people because it requires a ton of executive functioning and most of the tools that are readily available just don't work very well.

So... what can be done about this?

If you're made of money, you can hire a personal chef, get your meals delivered, or just eat out everyday.

 Ok... I get it. Take me to the Next section

But unfortunately, that's not a sustainable model for most people.

So cooking (or preparing food in some form) is typically the best option most of the time.

But again, cooking is hard and causes tons of stress and anxiety.

And shame spiraling.

To relieve the stress, anxiety and shame, we go out to eat anyway even if we can't afford it or prepare something we know isn't good for us.

And then often, we experience shame around that choice as well.

It's a vicious freakin' circle where it feels like whatever choice you make, you have to sacrifice something important.

Until today.

DUN DUN DUUUUN!!!! (dramatic sound effect)

Introducing... The Real-Life Executive Functioning Cookbook.

We spent hours and hours soul searching (at least 1 of the authors is neurodivergent), listened to pain points about cooking expressed by our coaching clients, and read through countless frustrations on online forums about everything that's not neurodivergent-friendly about traditional cookbooks.

From there, we came up with a list of everything we thought we could improve upon in a reasonable amount of time.

And we set out to do just that.

Below is everything we believe our cookbook delivers to the neurodivergent community (and anyone really) that traditional cookbooks don't... with more still to come.

My hope is that our cookbook will save you some money, time, assist you in developing an important life skill, and most importantly, make cooking accessible thereby helping you realize what you're capable of.

 take me to the COOKBOOK

WHAT MAKES THIS digital COOKBOOK NEURODIVERGENT-FRIENDLY?

Click here to view a sample recipe.

Zero jumping around

BASED ON

REAL LIFE

None of our recipes require you to jump to page 267 for the sauce or page 85 for the other sauce. All necessary steps are self-contained within each recipe.

Keeps you ahead of waiting PARALYSIS

TESTED IN

REAL LIFE

Overwhelmed or not sure what to do while waiting for the water to boil? We've included red bold text cues.

built in prep time

Our cookbook encourages you to retrieve all the ingredients & supplies and, when it makes sense, complete all the prep FIRST before even turning on a burner. Slower? Maybe. Less stressful and safer? Definitely.

Readiness cues

Do you sometimes ambitiously jump into a project without knowing what you're getting yourself into only to realize halfway though that you may be in over your head? Step 1 of every recipe is to "Read it Through".

Don't burn your house down reminders

Critical safety reminders like turning off the burner before walking away are called out so you don't burn your house down!

Expansion Ideas

Novelty is important! We've included a list of optional ingredients and variation ideas for each recipe in our book.

Photo examples for everything

Every step includes a photo.

Brain power meter

Look for our Brain Power Meter icons at the top of each recipe to quickly tell how much brain power it'll require.

Function First

Look... this isn't a cookbook that's going to teach you how to become Julia Child. This is a functional cookbook! While super tasty, we've intentionally prioritized recipes that anyone can cook.

Icons That Make Sense

At the top of each recipe, in addition to our Brain Power Meter, we've included a few other helpful icons to help you makes choices based on the situation, time, budget and more.

ACTION ITEMS IN BOLD 

Sometimes extra words are needed to help people understand what the hell we're talking about. Action items are always displayed in bold to help you focus in on what's most important.

CHAPTERS ORGANIZED BY

EF-DEMAND

While most cookbooks organize their chapters by cuisine, ours organizes by brain power. Running low on brain capacity? Try the "Three Ingredients or Less" chapter.

ALL INGREDIENTS ARE EASY TO FIND

No hunting down some super specific ingredient that you probably can't even tell the difference from the alternative anyway.

measurements are "split" from the beginning

You know how at the top of most cookbook recipes, they say something like "olive oil (split)" but don't tell you how much to split until you get way down to that step? That's annoying. Don't do that.

Portable & flexible

Pull the cookbook up on your phone or tablet or print out just the recipe you're working on.

ZERO PERSONAL ANECDOTES/LIFE STORIES

You're welcome.

Hi, I’m Chris and I was born and raised in Cleveland, Ohio. I moved to the Seattle area in September of 2008 and soon after, I met my awesome wife, Lisa!

I earned my special education teaching degree while working as paraeducator in the Kent School District. Overall, I have about 8 years of classroom experience and 20 years and counting of personal experience with ADHD and anxiety. I feel very grateful to be on the other side of it, supporting some amazing young adults.

With everything I do, my mission is to provide neurodivergent individuals and families with the life skills training, executive functioning support, mentorship & coaching they need to build and sustain autonomy & independence.

Which includes cooking!

I consider the Real-Life Executive Functioning Cookbook to be a natural extension of this mission.

Chris

Who is This Cookbook For?

In short, anyone can benefit from our cookbook.

However, it was specially-designed for neurodivergent individuals who struggle with executive functioning.

We believe the Real-Life Executive Functioning Cookbook is also a great tool for parents, educators, coaches, and anyone who supports neurodivergent individuals.

How Many Recipes Are Included?

20 (and countless variation)

Is a physical copy Available Somewhere?

Not at this time. And we're not sure if there ever will be. All the options we've explored so far require us to give up either a huge chunk of each sale or creative control. We're not interested in doing either.

If you know of a better way to publish or self-publish, we're all ears. Reach out to me at chris@lifeskillsadvocate.com.

Can/Should I Print This Cookbook Then?

You certainly can. After purchase, the cookbook will be delivered to you as a .pdf file, and if printing is the best format for you, we'd recommend doing so.

Can I freely Distribute This Cookbook?

You are more than welcome to use our cookbook with yourself, your family, and the learners your support, however, I must ask that you NOT share it with your colleagues or other people. As well-intentioned as doing so may be, making copies of and sharing any paid product is considered stealing. We are a small company and the sales generated from this cookbook enable us to fund many of the free resources found on our website dedicated to supporting neurodiverse learners, families & professionals.

If you wish to purchase multiple cookbook licenses for your organization, please reach out to me directly at chris@lifeskillsadvocate.com and we can discuss bulk license discount options. Thank you!

Do You Accept Purchase Orders?

Yes, if your school or organization would like to purchase single or bulk licenses via purchase order, please email chris@lifeskillsadvocate.com.

What is Your Refund Policy?

You are fully protected by our 100% Satisfaction-Guarantee. If you aren't satisfied within 7 days of purchase, just let us know and we'll send you a prompt refund.

Who Can I Contact if I have questions?

Reach out anytime by emailing chris@lifeskillsadvocate.com.
